scope: Permit bounded engineering renewal I/O up to45s inside the existing60s acknowledged lease; preserve legacy30s/25s and every immutable deadline, revocation and source boundary.
riskAnalysis: A longer I/O wait must not extend authority. Bound end by last acknowledged lease minus1s, task/operation expiry and cancellation; reject late or malformed acknowledgments and malformed explicit budgets; preserve pre-CAS elapsed-wall guards and shutdown.

threatModel.assets: Owner authority, immutable task/release identity, ledger integrity, cancellation and pending provider exposure.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Waiting for authenticated renewal versus granting extended execution authority; acknowledged lease versus untrusted late callbacks.
threatModel.abuseCases: Expired/revoked authority, late acknowledgment after timeout, null/coerced budgets, overlapping renewals, ignored cancellation or replay after failed dispatch.
threatModel.mitigations: Engineering-only45s I/O default with unchanged60s lease and min(lastACK-1s,expiry,operation) deadline, exact undefined-only default, pre-CAS checks, no overlap/retry, revoke/readback on every failure.

defects.rootCause: One actual Chief-stage renewal exceeded the25s I/O allowance despite an existing60s engineering lease. Total26313ms and finalledger-cas2462ms are observed; the remaining latency and whether all slow cases fit45s are not established.
defects.detectionGap: Earlier16.1s real-timer regression proved the old allowance only for that lower latency, not the observed26.313s case.
defects.regression: Virtual observed26313ms and actual26.5s success inside60s; legacy25s rejection; lateACK/expiry/cancel/malformed-budget denials; existing pre-CAS wall deadline, diagnostics, no-overlap and five-stage fixtures.
defects.historicalPrevention: Derive I/O bounds from the distinct acknowledged lease policy and observed latency while preserving absolute deadlines; include delayed and expired-ack fixtures rather than treating fixture speed as hosted proof.

rollback: Keep paid execution off and all grants revoked; preserve failedcount/request bookkeeping and uncertainty. Revert through a reviewed successor only; never reuse the failed approval or rewrite historical evidence.
